{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Morris Iemma ( ; born 21 July 1961) is a former Australian politician who was the 40th Premier of New South Wales, serving from 3 August 2005 to 5 September 2008.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" From Sydney, Iemma attended the University of Sydney and the University of Technology, Sydney.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" A member of the Labor Party, he was first elected to the Parliament of New South Wales at the 1991 state election, having previously worked as a trade union official.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" From 1999, Iemma was a minister in the third and fourth ministries led by Bob Carr.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" He replaced Carr as premier and Leader of the New South Wales Labor Party in 2005, following Carr's resignation.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Iemma led Labor to victory at the 2007 state election, albeit with a slightly reduced majority.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" He resigned as premier in 2008, after losing the support of caucus, and left parliament shortly after, triggering a by-election.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" He was replaced as premier by Nathan Rees.","title":"Morris Iemma"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"A by-election was held for the New South Wales Legislative Assembly seat of Lakemba on 18 October 2008 after former Premier Morris Iemma resigned as member for Lakemba.","title":"Lakemba state by-election, 2008"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It coincided with the Cabramatta, Port Macquarie and Ryde by-elections.","title":"Lakemba state by-election, 2008"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"Morris Iemma's replacement as Premier of New South Wales was born on what date?"}
